issues.legal_issue: A deed whose operative terms create a loan secured by property, provide for redemption, and allocate interest and possession is a mortgage rather than an outright sale.
material_facts: The registered deed described the transaction as a mortgage and stated that the property secured money advanced.
It provided for redemption and addressed interest, rent, possession, and repair costs.
A later unregistered document was relied on to argue that the transaction was actually an outright sale.
issues.conclusion: The registered deed, considered on its own, was a mortgage deed and not a sale deed.
issues.legal_principle: The nature of an instrument is determined from its terms. The Court found that the terms of the registered deed clearly created a mortgage; it cited no earlier case or statutory provision for this construction.

predicates.mortgage_or_sale_classification_dispute: The case involves a dispute over whether a deed creates a mortgage or an outright sale.
predicates.deed_secures_loan: The deed states that property is given as security for money advanced.
predicates.deed_provides_for_redemption: The deed gives the transferor a right to recover the property by paying the secured amount.

issues.definition: When a deed is disputed as a mortgage or sale and it secures a loan and provides for redemption, the deed is treated as a mortgage.

issues.legal_issue: An unregistered instrument that is required to be registered under the property-transfer law cannot be used as evidence of a transaction affecting the immovable property it concerns.
material_facts: The later document was relied on to establish that the transaction involving the house was an outright sale and to read it together with the registered mortgage deed.
The later document was unregistered, although the sale it purported to record required registration.
The document was offered as evidence of a transaction affecting immovable property.
issues.conclusion: The unregistered document was inadmissible as evidence of the transaction affecting the property and could not be read with the registered deed to establish an outright sale.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 4 and 54 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, read with section 49 of the Registration Act, 1908, as amended by section 10 of the Transfer of Property (Amendment) Supplementary Act, 1929, required registration and barred an unregistered document from being received as evidence of a transaction affecting the property. The amendment made clear that section 49 covered documents requiring registration under the Transfer of Property Act even when not independently covered by section 17 of the Registration Act. The Court referred to Sohan Lal v. Mohan Lal and Rama Sahu v. Gowro Ratho as earlier decisions reflecting a contrary view, which the subsequent legislation had superseded.

predicates.unregistered_property_transaction_docume: A party relies on a document concerning a transaction affecting immovable property, and the document has not been registered.
predicates.registration_required_for_property_trans: The kind of property transaction recorded in the document requires registration.
predicates.offered_to_prove_property_transaction: A party offers the document as evidence that the transaction affecting the property occurred or had a particular nature.

issues.definition: When an unregistered document records a property transaction that requires registration and is offered to prove that transaction, it is inadmissible for that purpose.

issues.legal_issue: A higher court cannot grant a plaintiff relief beyond that granted by the trial court when the plaintiff did not appeal the trial court's decree seeking that additional relief.
material_facts: The trial court granted redemption on stated terms.
The plaintiff did not appeal the trial court's decree seeking a direction for the defendants to render accounts before claiming payment.
The High Court restored the trial court's decree but added a direction that the defendants render accounts before claiming payment.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's additional direction for the defendants to render accounts was set aside because the plaintiff had not appealed the trial court's decree to obtain that further relief.
issues.legal_principle: In appellate proceedings, a court is not legally justified in granting a plaintiff further relief than the trial court granted when the plaintiff did not appeal the trial court's decree seeking that relief. The Court cited no statutory provision or earlier case for this ruling.

predicates.civil_appeal_from_trial_decree: The matter is before a higher court in an appeal concerning a civil decree.
predicates.plaintiff_did_not_appeal_for_additional_: The plaintiff did not appeal the trial court's decree seeking the additional relief later granted.
predicates.appellate_court_granted_greater_relief: The higher court granted the plaintiff relief beyond what the trial court had granted.

issues.definition: In a civil appeal, if the plaintiff did not appeal for additional relief and the higher court grants relief beyond the trial court's decree, that additional relief must be set aside.
